meta.name: F9-class parametric reusable booster: baseline parameter database
meta.research_question: For a reusable LOX/RP-1 booster, which engine cluster size maximizes payload to a fixed target orbit at constant total liftoff thrust, when accounting for engine dry mass, minimum-throttle limits, and propellant required for downrange recovery?
meta.units: SI throughout (N, kg, m, s, Pa). Angles in degrees only where noted.

source_types.official: SpaceX publication (Falcon User's Guide, spacex.com, SpaceX posts)
source_types.peer_reviewed: Journal or peer-reviewed paper; note that Dresia et al. 2021 state their Falcon 9 numbers are unofficial estimates
source_types.secondary: Reputable secondary source (e.g., NASASpaceFlight quoting SpaceX)
source_types.unofficial: Community or aggregator estimate (Wikipedia, Wevolver, forums)
source_types.derived: Calculated by us from other values in this file
source_types.assumption: Engineering assumption chosen by the research team; must be swept in sensitivity runs

sources.S11: Kyle, E., SpaceX Falcon 9 v1.2 Data Sheet (Space Launch Report), hosted by NASA SMA. https://sma.nasa.gov/LaunchVehicle/assets/spacex-falcon-9-v1.2-data-sheet.pdf

supplement.name: Supplement to parameters_baseline.json: values the database states only in prose, plus model idealizations
supplement.policy: Every entry here is an ASSUMPTION or is quoted from a used_for/notes/range field of parameters_baseline.json. Each is listed in docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md. Nothing here is published data.

parameters.name: engine.total_sl_thrust
parameters.used_for: Held constant for every engine count N. Per-engine sea-level thrust = T_tot_sl / N.
parameters.notes: S1 Table 2-1 lists 7,686 kN (9 x 854 kN, carried over from 2021 guide typo). 190,000 lbf = 845 kN, so use 7,605 kN.
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf

parameters.name: engine.reference_engine_count
parameters.used_for: Calibration point for all mass models (Falcon 9 has 9 Merlin 1D engines).
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf

parameters.name: engine.vac_to_sl_thrust_ratio
parameters.used_for: Vacuum thrust per engine = r_vs x sea-level thrust. Sets the nozzle exit area via (T_vac - T_sl)/p0.
parameters.notes: No current official vacuum thrust for the sea-level Merlin.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: engine.isp_sl
parameters.used_for: Sea-level performance; with Isp_vac defines mass flow and exit area.
parameters.notes: SpaceX publishes no Isp for the sea-level Merlin. Check internal consistency with r_vs and Isp_vac (they are ~2% inconsistent as a set); report how you resolve it.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: engine.isp_vac
parameters.used_for: Mass flow = T_vac / (g0 * Isp_vac).
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: engine.min_throttle_sl_thrust_fraction
parameters.used_for: Minimum throttle. Defined as a fraction of RATED SEA-LEVEL THRUST at sea level (that is how SpaceX states it). If the code throttles on mass flow with a pressure-thrust term, convert this to the equivalent mass-flow fraction.
parameters.notes: 0.70 = 2013 early Merlin 1D (S12, quoting SpaceX). ~0.40 appears only on forums (unverified) and is a sensitivity case only.
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf | S2: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, Sept 2021. https://web.mit.edu/2.70/Reading%20Materials/SpaceX%20Falcon-users-guide-2021-09.pdf

parameters.name: engine.max_throttle
parameters.used_for: Upper throttle bound (no over-throttle).

parameters.name: engine.engine_restart
parameters.used_for: Entry and landing burns are allowed.
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf

parameters.name: engine.reference_engine_dry_mass
parameters.used_for: Engine mass at the reference point (845 kN SL). All engine-mass models are calibrated to this point.
parameters.notes: Range corresponds to sea-level thrust-to-weight 150-200 (S12 states vacuum T/W > 150; S1 says 'highest of any boost engine').
parameters.source_description: S13: Wikipedia pages: SpaceX Merlin, Falcon 9, Falcon 9 Full Thrust (accessed Nov 2026)

parameters.name: engine.engine_mass_model
parameters.used_for: m_e(N) = m_ref * [phi + (1 - phi) * (N_ref / N)^beta]. Alternatives to run as sensitivity: 'akin_scaled' (see akin_* below).
parameters.notes: Generic MERs overpredict Merlin 1D mass 1.8-2.7x, so every MER must be calibrated to m_ref at 845 kN.

parameters.name: engine.fixed_mass_fraction
parameters.source: derived from S7 (Akin MER fixed term 59 kg, scaled by 0.56 so the MER matches 470 kg: 33 kg / 470 kg)
parameters.used_for: Share of engine mass that does not shrink when the engine gets smaller (valves, igniters, controller, harness).
parameters.source_description: S7: Akin, D. L., Mass Estimating Relations, ENAE 791 lecture notes, Univ. of Maryland, 2016. https://spacecraft.ssl.umd.edu/academics/791S16/791S16L08.MERsx.pdf

parameters.name: engine.mass_scaling_exponent
parameters.used_for: How engine mass scales with per-engine thrust. beta = 1 means no clustering mass penalty beyond the fixed part.

parameters.name: engine.akin_mer_coefficients
parameters.used_for: Alternative engine-mass model ('akin_scaled'). Multiply by the calibration scale so it equals m_ref at 845 kN and Ae/At = 16; verify the scale in code rather than trusting 0.56.
parameters.source_description: S7: Akin, D. L., Mass Estimating Relations, ENAE 791 lecture notes, Univ. of Maryland, 2016. https://spacecraft.ssl.umd.edu/academics/791S16/791S16L08.MERsx.pdf

parameters.name: engine.nozzle_expansion_ratio
parameters.used_for: Only used inside the Akin MER. Exit area itself comes from r_vs.

parameters.name: engine.thrust_structure_coefficient
parameters.used_for: Thrust structure mass = k_ts * T_tot. Independent of N, so it is part of the non-engine mass, not a clustering penalty.
parameters.notes: Do not double count: this is already inside the 26 t booster dry mass at N = 9.
parameters.source_description: S7: Akin, D. L., Mass Estimating Relations, ENAE 791 lecture notes, Univ. of Maryland, 2016. https://spacecraft.ssl.umd.edu/academics/791S16/791S16L08.MERsx.pdf

parameters.name: engine.per_engine_integration_mass
parameters.source: assumption (no published relationship ties thrust-structure mass to engine count)
parameters.used_for: Extra stage-side mass per engine (mounts, gimbal actuators, feed lines, harness). This is a clustering penalty.

parameters.name: engine.entry_burn_engines
parameters.used_for: Falcon 9 practice at N = 9. For other N, use the rule written in the prompt (match the thrust fraction 3/9 as closely as allowed, respect acceleration cap).
parameters.source_description: S9: Zilker, F., Aerothermal Analysis of Re-usable First Stage during Rocket Retro-propulsion, M.Sc. thesis, Univ. Stuttgart/DLR, 2018. https://elib.dlr.de/119265/1/SADA_ITLR.pdf | S11: Kyle, E., SpaceX Falcon 9 v1.2 Data Sheet (Space Launch Report), hosted by NASA SMA. https://sma.nasa.gov/LaunchVehicle/assets/spacex-falcon-9-v1.2-data-sheet.pdf

parameters.name: engine.landing_burn_engines_allowed
parameters.source: S11, S9 (1 engine usual; 3-engine landing burns have been flown)
parameters.used_for: Allowed numbers of engines lit for the landing burn, for odd N (center engine plus symmetric pairs).
parameters.source_description: S9: Zilker, F., Aerothermal Analysis of Re-usable First Stage during Rocket Retro-propulsion, M.Sc. thesis, Univ. Stuttgart/DLR, 2018. https://elib.dlr.de/119265/1/SADA_ITLR.pdf | S11: Kyle, E., SpaceX Falcon 9 v1.2 Data Sheet (Space Launch Report), hosted by NASA SMA. https://sma.nasa.gov/LaunchVehicle/assets/spacex-falcon-9-v1.2-data-sheet.pdf

parameters.name: booster.glow_full_vehicle
parameters.used_for: Calibration target at N = 9 and maximum liftoff mass constraint.
parameters.notes: Treated as vehicle mass WITHOUT payload (assumption; SpaceX does not say). Dresia S5 gives 569.3 t; their split does not add up to the official total.
parameters.source_description: S3: SpaceX, Falcon 9 vehicle page. https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9

parameters.name: booster.dry_mass_at_reference
parameters.source: between S5 (27.2 t) and S19 (25.6 t); community 22-27 t
parameters.used_for: Booster dry mass at N = 9 INCLUDING engines, thrust structure and recovery hardware. Non-engine mass = m_d_ref - 9*(m_ref + m_int); hold that non-engine mass fixed for all N.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: booster.recovery_hardware_fraction
parameters.source: S5 uses +15% of dry mass; S6 scales legs/fins linearly with dry mass
parameters.used_for: Legs + grid fins share of booster dry mass. Already inside m_d_ref. Remove it only for the EXPENDABLE calibration case.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates) | S6: Stappert, S. et al., Assessment of a European Reusable VTVL Booster Stage, Space Propulsion 2018, SP2018_00478. https://elib.dlr.de/121410/2/478_STAPPERT.pdf

parameters.name: booster.propellant_capacity
parameters.source: derived: 549,054 (S3) - 26,000 booster dry - 4,500 upper dry - 111,500 upper prop - 2,400 payload bay = 404,654 kg, ASSUMING SpaceX's 549,054 kg excludes payload (SpaceX does not say). S5 estimate is 418.7 t; the research report's 411 t did not close.
parameters.used_for: Booster tank capacity (same tanks for every N). Recompute in code from the final baseline values so the N = 9 vehicle closes to 549,054 kg without payload, and log the result.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: booster.diameter
parameters.used_for: Reference area A = pi*D^2/4 for ascent and descent drag.
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf | S3: SpaceX, Falcon 9 vehicle page. https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9

parameters.name: booster.descent_drag_coefficient
parameters.source: assumption (no published numeric value in the sources reviewed; RETALT S20 has an open Mach-dependent database)
parameters.used_for: Engines-first descent drag. Sweep it.
parameters.source_description: S20: Marwege, A. et al., RETALT: review of technologies and overview of design changes, CEAS Space Journal, 2022 (open aerodynamic database)

parameters.name: booster.ascent_drag_coefficient_table
parameters.used_for: Full-stack ascent drag. Same for every N, so it mostly cancels in comparisons.

parameters.name: upper_stage.vac_thrust
parameters.used_for: Upper-stage thrust (Merlin Vacuum).
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf | S3: SpaceX, Falcon 9 vehicle page. https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9

parameters.name: upper_stage.isp_vac
parameters.used_for: Upper-stage mass flow.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: upper_stage.burn_time
parameters.used_for: Consistency check only: 981 kN / (g0 * 348 s) * 397 s = 114.1 t, vs 111.5 t propellant below (~2% mismatch). Report it; do not hide it.
parameters.source_description: S3: SpaceX, Falcon 9 vehicle page. https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9

parameters.name: upper_stage.dry_mass
parameters.used_for: Upper-stage dry mass.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: upper_stage.propellant
parameters.used_for: Upper-stage propellant (fixed for every N).
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: upper_stage.min_throttle
parameters.used_for: Only needed if the upper stage throttles for an acceleration limit.
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf

parameters.name: upper_stage.payload_bay_overhead
parameters.source: derived from S5 (7.4 t payload bay for 5.0 t payload)
parameters.used_for: Fairing + adapter + avionics bay. Baseline: jettison the fairing portion (assume 1,900 kg of the 2,400) when dynamic pressure falls below 10 Pa, keep the rest to orbit. State this choice.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: mission.target_orbit_altitude
parameters.source: research team choice; matches S5 LEO case and the secondary-source basis of the 22.8 t figure
parameters.used_for: Circular insertion target: r = R_E + h_orb, radial velocity 0, inertial horizontal velocity = sqrt(mu/r).
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: mission.target_inclination_deg
parameters.source: S1 Table 3-1 (Eastern Range minimum without penalty)
parameters.used_for: Due-east launch; Earth rotation boost = omega_E * R_E * cos(latitude).
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf

parameters.name: mission.launch_site_latitude_deg
parameters.used_for: Earth rotation velocity at launch.
parameters.source_description: S2: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, Sept 2021. https://web.mit.edu/2.70/Reading%20Materials/SpaceX%20Falcon-users-guide-2021-09.pdf

parameters.name: mission.max_dynamic_pressure
parameters.source: unofficial proxy (SpaceX does not publish max-Q)
parameters.used_for: Ascent constraint (report it; allow a throttle bucket only if needed and identical logic for every N).

parameters.name: mission.ascent_axial_accel_cap_g
parameters.source: assumption bounded by S14 telemetry (3.43 g peak) and S2 limit loads (6 g)
parameters.used_for: Ascent acceleration limit; S2 says first and second stage engines may be throttled to hold steady-state acceleration limits.
parameters.source_description: S2: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, Sept 2021. https://web.mit.edu/2.70/Reading%20Materials/SpaceX%20Falcon-users-guide-2021-09.pdf | S14: shahar603, Telemetry-Data (webcast-extracted), GitHub

parameters.name: mission.earth_model
parameters.used_for: Spherical Earth, inverse-square gravity, rotating atmosphere for drag.

parameters.name: mission.atmosphere_model
parameters.value: US Standard Atmosphere 1976 (0-86 km), exponential above
parameters.used_for: Density, pressure, speed of sound.
parameters.baseline_value: US Standard Atmosphere 1976 (0-86 km), exponential above

parameters.name: recovery.recovery_mode
parameters.used_for: Drone ship is placed at the predicted impact point, so horizontal touchdown position is free; touchdown speed must be ~0.

parameters.name: recovery.entry_burn_start_altitude
parameters.source: S9 (entry burn 70 to 36 km), S6 (F9 about 50 km)
parameters.used_for: Entry burn starts on the descending leg at this altitude (or at apogee if apogee is lower).
parameters.source_description: S6: Stappert, S. et al., Assessment of a European Reusable VTVL Booster Stage, Space Propulsion 2018, SP2018_00478. https://elib.dlr.de/121410/2/478_STAPPERT.pdf | S9: Zilker, F., Aerothermal Analysis of Re-usable First Stage during Rocket Retro-propulsion, M.Sc. thesis, Univ. Stuttgart/DLR, 2018. https://elib.dlr.de/119265/1/SADA_ITLR.pdf

parameters.name: recovery.entry_severity_limit_peak_q
parameters.source: CALIBRATED at N = 9 (see prompt); DLR model bound q < 200 kPa (S6) is an upper bound only
parameters.used_for: Entry burn is sized so that peak dynamic pressure after the burn stays below this value.

parameters.name: recovery.landing_max_accel_g
parameters.source: S17 (DLR: landing T/W above 3 treated as infeasible)
parameters.used_for: Landing-burn acceleration cap; checked over the whole burn (it peaks near touchdown when mass is lowest).
parameters.source_description: S17: DLR SART: Sippel et al. IAF 2022 (https://elib.dlr.de/195201/1/IAF22-2.pdf); SLME studies, Space Propulsion 2022

parameters.name: recovery.touchdown_speed_max
parameters.used_for: Touchdown speed tolerance.

parameters.name: recovery.landing_propellant_margin
parameters.source: assumption (S5 uses 5% margin inside its landing delta-v)
parameters.used_for: Extra propellant carried beyond nominal entry + landing burns; stays on board (affects dynamics).

parameters.name: recovery.residual_propellant
parameters.used_for: Unusable trapped propellant at touchdown.

parameters.name: validation_targets.expendable_leo_payload
parameters.notes: SpaceX does not state the orbit; secondary sources: ~200 km from the Cape. Use as calibration anchor at N = 9 (expendable).
parameters.source_description: S3: SpaceX, Falcon 9 vehicle page. https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9

parameters.name: validation_targets.reusable_drone_ship_leo_payload
parameters.notes: Starlink orbits are not exactly 200 km circular; treat as approximate. Quoted capability 17.5-18.5 t is unofficial (S13).
parameters.source_description: S16: SpaceX post on X, 26 Jan 2023 (Starlink 5-2: more than 17.4 t, heaviest payload flown on Falcon, booster landed on drone ship)

parameters.name: validation_targets.landing_propellant_estimate
parameters.source: S5 Table A1 (unofficial, GTO 5 t mission)
parameters.notes: Plausibility check only, not a calibration target: S5 is a GTO case with faster staging than LEO.
parameters.source_description: S5: Dresia, K. et al., Multidisciplinary Design Optimization of Reusable Launch Vehicles for Different Propellants and Objectives, J. Spacecraft and Rockets 58(4):1017-1029, 2021, doi:10.2514/1.A34944 (Falcon 9 data in Table A1 are unofficial estimates)

parameters.name: validation_targets.landing_tw_at_min_throttle_N9
parameters.source: derived from S1 (482 kN) and 27-30 t landing mass
parameters.notes: Sanity check for the thrust model at N = 9.
parameters.source_description: S1: SpaceX, Falcon User's Guide, v8 (March 2025), file dated 2025-05-09. https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf

parameters.name: upper_stage.fairing_jettison_mass
parameters.used_for: Part of m_bay dropped at fairing jettison; the remainder (m_bay - m_fair = 500 kg at baseline) goes to orbit.
parameters.notes: Range = JSON m_bay range (1,700-2,600 kg) minus the 500 kg retained part. Not swept in this study.

parameters.name: upper_stage.fairing_jettison_dynamic_pressure
parameters.source: parameters_baseline.json upper_stage.payload_bay_overhead.used_for ('when dynamic pressure falls below 10 Pa')
parameters.used_for: Fairing is jettisoned at the first downward crossing of q = q_fair after liftoff.
parameters.notes: Prescribed by the team's JSON; not swept.

parameters.name: booster.ascent_cd_scale
parameters.used_for: Multiplies the ascent Cd(M) table. Calibration knob 1 (expendable N = 9 payload anchor).
parameters.notes: Value is replaced by the calibrated value in every production run; see results/*/manifest.json.

parameters.name: recovery.entry_q_window
parameters.source: prompt section 6.4.2 ('peak dynamic pressure afterward'); parameters_baseline.json recovery.entry_severity_limit_peak_q.used_for
parameters.used_for: Window over which q_entry_max is enforced: 'after_burn' = only the aerodynamic descent after the entry burn (literal wording, BASELINE); 'burn_and_after' = from entry-burn start to the ground, so q experienced during a long low-thrust burn also counts.

parameters.name: recovery.landing_accel_cap_basis
parameters.used_for: Which acceleration the landing cap a_max_land limits: 'thrust_plus_drag' = |T + D|/m (database definition, BASELINE) or 'thrust_only' = T/m (DLR-style T/W reading of S17; alternative for the team to decide).
parameters.notes: Switch exists because the database definition makes N = 9 unable to land (see docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md A-CAP).

parameters.name: mission.launch_pad_altitude
parameters.source: assumption (pad at sea level; SLC-40 pad elevation is not in the database)
parameters.used_for: Initial altitude of the ascent and the landing (drone-ship deck) altitude.
parameters.notes: Drone-ship deck height and pad elevation (a few metres) are neglected.
